perf.summary: Each popped node rescans all states to find children, making link-tree traversal O(stateCount^2).
perf.currentCost: For every node popped (stateCount of them) the inner loop scans linkPtr[0..stateCount) to find i with linkPtr[i]==v. Total O(stateCount^2) loads and branches even though the link tree has exactly stateCount-1 edges.
perf.proposedChange: Precompute a children adjacency in CSR form once: count children per parent (one pass over linkPtr), prefix-sum into head offsets, scatter child indices into a flat int* childBuf. Then traversal visits each node and iterates only its real children -> O(stateCount). Accept the two scratch buffers (childHead[stateCount+1], childBuf[stateCount]) as caller-provided pointers to honor the no-alloc rule.
perf.rationale: Reduces traversal from O(n^2) to O(n) with two linear passes; for n in the thousands this is orders of magnitude fewer memory accesses and far better cache behavior (sequential CSR scans vs repeated full-array sweeps).
perf.risk: Pure restructuring of iteration order; DFS visit set is identical. Visit ORDER changes (children grouped by parent rather than reverse-scan order) — if callback ordering is observable to callers, document it. Requires extra scratch buffers passed in by the caller.
